defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: The 3D viewport shows the scene, and the outliner lists what is in it.
Object Mode moves whole objects, and Edit Mode changes the mesh itself.
Engines budget by triangles, while Blender shows the face count.
The origin is where an object is measured from, the pivot what it turns around.
Apply transforms so the mesh carries the real size and scale reads one, one, one.
A material is the whole surface recipe, and a texture is one image it uses.
bookends.command: Quiz me on Blender modeling terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms Object Mode, Edit Mode, origin, pivot, apply transforms, face count, triangle count, modifier, material and texture. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me whether I was right.
checks: Check: every case is a modeling task from a game, and the answer waits.
Check: you gave the exact term and said why the look-alike does not fit.
